title: Rigorous Formulation of Finite-Sample and Finite-Window Effects in Galaxy Clustering
summary: Galaxy surveys provide finite catalogs of objects observed within bounded volumes, yet clustering statistics are often interpreted using theoretical frameworks developed for infinite point processes. In this work, we formulate key statistical quantities directly for finite point processes and examine the structural consequences of finite-number and finite-window constraints. We show that several well-known features of galaxy survey analysis arise naturally from finiteness alone.
